thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-postgres (high urgency). Rule=DB_CONN_DEGRADATION. summary=connection accept queue growing > 1000.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident created -> PD-2451. Escalation policy=eng-oncall-primary.
jamie: acked PD-2451, I'm on it. seeing customer 5xxs for embedding writes and some timeouts. marking channel primary for coordination.
mike: on my way, giving context: last deploy 30m ago touched pgbouncer config (pool_mode=transaction) but shouldn't affect accepts. metrics showing pg_accept_queue length spiking.
sara: adding metrics: pg_exporter shows active_connections 1200, max_connections 300, accept_queue 1024, pg_stat_activity rows waiting on lock ~800. Redis metrics normal but some frontend cache misses up.
lee: can you post top queries? any long-running DDLs?
jamie: grabbing quick snapshot from primary:
```
SELECT state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state;
-- results: active=350, idle=40, idle in transaction=610, waiting=190
SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS dur, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY dur DESC LIMIT 10;
-- many entries stuck as "idle in transaction" from worker processes.
```
jamie: stack traces from app show many requests blocking on DB connection acquisition; app-level pool timeout 10s.
mike: hypothesis: connection leak or pgbouncer routing issue causing accept backlog at kernel level, clients stuck in socket accept queue. Could be pgbouncer stuck or file descriptor exhaustion.
sara: checking pgbouncer on all app nodes: IS_HEALTHY but stats show cl_active=0, cl_waiting high on one host (app-11). pgbouncer on app-11 shows client connections=1024 (maxclients), others 50-100.
lee: rolling pgbouncer on app-11 may relieve pressure. but need safe sequence to avoid cascading failures.
jamie: mitigation plan:
  1) divert new traffic to standby region for non-critical writes (enable routing->fallback to read-only where possible)
  2) restart pgbouncer on app-11 gracefully (disable new connections, wait for leases, then bounce)
  3) increase pgbouncer max_client_conn temporarily and throttle high-volume jobs
  4) inspect long-lived transactions and kill ones that are idle-in-transaction > 5m
  5) if accept_queue persists, rotate primary to read replica (failover) as last resort
mike: I'll do pgbouncer restart on app-11. running:
```
sudo systemctl stop pgbouncer
sleep 3
sudo systemctl start pgbouncer
```
mike: initiating now, removing app-11 from LB first (maintenance mode).
jamie: marking LB rule to remove app-11 -> done.
mike: pgbouncer stopped, waiting 15s, starting now.
mike: pgbouncer back up on app-11. stats: client_conn dropped from 1024 -> 200. accept_queue reported down to ~50.
sara: clearing stuck idle transactions: listing pids where state='idle in transaction' older than 5m.
```
SELECT pid FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='idle in transaction' AND now() - xact_start > interval '5 minutes';
```
mike: I'm killing top offenders (via pg_terminate_backend) in batches of 10 to avoid lock storms.
mike: killed 36 sessions. seeing immediate drop in waiting and accept_queue.
jamie: app errors dropping—5xx rate down to baseline. customers still seeing a small backlog for in-flight writes; we'll monitor.
lee: root cause notes: app pool misbehaving + one overloaded pgbouncer instance + a couple of transactions held open by a background job. Will file RCA later.
sara: creating short incident summary for PD-2451 and tagging customers with relevant SLO impact. severity=high->customer-impact: partial write latencies increased; some retries triggered. estimated affected customers: ~12 orgs on heavy write paths.
mike: before we close, increase pgbouncer max_client_conn to 2000 across nodes as interim? risk: more DB connections -> degrade primary.
jamie: don't touch DB max_connections. instead I suggest applying connection pooling tuning: set pgbouncer max_client_conn=800 and tune pool_size per app. we'll patch via config rollout in 10m.
lee: agree. I'll prepare config PR and roll canary on two nodes first.
incident-bot: PD-2451 acknowledged by jamie at 2245678911. Current status: mitigation in progress.
jamie: handoff: I'm stepping off in 30m. mike will lead continued mitigation and postmortem. mike, do you want the formal handoff?
mike: I can take lead. jamie, please add notes on the kill candidates and which transactions were terminated.
jamie: done. notes: killed pids [4523,4527,4531...] (logged in incident). Also linked logs -> https://logs.redwood.internal/PD-2451
mike: updating incident status to monitoring. will keep channel open for 1h then hand to daylight SRE.
lee: quick follow-ups: (1) add alert for pgbouncer client_conn > 800 on any single host, (2) add alert for idle in transaction > 60
sara: copied into ticket: RED-2451, adding runbook changes.
jamie: thanks all. :thumbsup: closing PD alert when confirmed stable. last check in 15m.
pd-bot: PD-2451 status updated -> monitoring
mike: observed steady metrics for 20m, accept_queue near 0, waiting queries < 10. marking incident for downgrade to incident-note.
jamie: last_message: handing off to mike for watch. leaving channel.
summary: PagerDuty PD-2451: Postgres accept queue spike due to overloaded pgbouncer and idle-in-transaction leak; pgbouncer restart & selective backend kills relieved backlog, mitigation ongoing; oncall handoff from jamie to mike.
